winner_in_my_two: STUDY MARKED: LOST — 3rd beaten 1L at SP 6/1 (banked 4/1; drifted 9/2 to 6/1 — the board moved AGAINST him and I could not see it); paper level stake −1.00
error: WINNER: Turty Tree 20/1 (Balding/Probert, OR 90, 9-0 in cheekpieces, drawn 4) beat Decade Of Time 7/1 (my SECOND danger) a head, Archers Bay 3/4L back in 3rd; Balding also 4th (Lord d'Or 33/1) and 5th (Cape Fear 22/1) — the yard's three pace-pressers filled 1-4-5; Heyzoom 5/4F (my NAMED danger) 8th of 9 beaten 27L; Into The Light last
calibration: winner_in_my_two: NO — my two were Archers Bay and Heyzoom; the second danger (Decade Of Time) was 2nd; the winner sat on my own BLANCO LINE (RP 96, within 4lb of the top) and I PASSED him on one bare fact, '6th LTO', without reading the run
column8: ERROR (one sentence): I passed the winner off the Blanco line on a single unread fact ('6th LTO') while the sheet's own collateral line — Decade Of Time beat Archers Bay 2L at Newmarket, 'the line still favours Decade Of Time by a length' — finished 2nd and 3rd exactly as written, and I backed the horse the line said was a length WORSE because he had the longer story (a C&D win, a Listed place) — the volume-over-weight fault a third time today, in a different coat
column9: CALIBRATION: (1) THE 7lb RISE WAS A FACT AND IT BIT: the sheet said 'if the handicapper has him, the top weight stops a furlong out; that caution is a FACT not a question, a LEAN by law 5d' — he was 3rd, beaten a length, carrying 135lb against a winner on 126; the law was right and the lean was wrong: when the caution is a FACT the sheet should PASS or take the collateral horse, not lean on the pick. (2) THE NAMED DANGER WAS THE MARKET'S MIRAGE: Heyzoom 5/4 (from 15/8), the 'unexposed Dubawi with the improver's floor', finished 8th beaten 27L — the bookmaker's question I asked ('why is a once-a-handicap-4th 15/8?') had the right suspicion and I still named him the danger instead of the collateral horse; the Haydock lesson (the unexposed floor is unbounded) does NOT say 'the unexposed favourite wins' — it says READ THE TELL: here the tell (top yard, number-one rider, big-day booking) was absent — Saffie Osborne, a 79-day absence, a yard with no freshness receipt — and I let the name of the sire do the reading. (3) THE BLANCO LINE MUST BE READ, NOT COUNTED: three horses within 4lb were PASSED on one word each (6th LTO / 11th as fav / 3-7-8); one of the passed won at 20/1; a pass on the Blanco line needs the RUN read (why 6th), not the number. (4) THE DRAW: the result's DBI says stalls 1-3 returned 70% and Archers Bay was drawn 8 of 9 (high) — I did not read the draw at Ascot 1m4f (round course) at all; the winner 4, the second 1. (5) BALDING TREBLE-HANDED, 1-4-5 at 20/1, 33/1, 22/1: three runners from one yard in a 9-runner heritage handicap, all pace-pressers — REPORT for his word: the multiple-runners tell (which of a yard's several is the intended one — the first-time headgear, the top jockey) is not read anywhere in the system. (6) The board: banked 4/1, SP 6/1 — the market drifted him 50% in 30 minutes; the sitting cannot see the board, the box can (law 4g) — the drift was the crowd saying what the 7lb said. (7) THE PAST WINNERS (his paste, nine runnings 2017-2025): winning weights 8-3, 9-6, 8-8, 9-0, 9-3, 8-5, 8-8, 8-12, 8-12 — NOT ONE winner above 9-6 in nine years, and Archers Bay carried 9-9 as TOP WEIGHT; Balding/Probert won it in 2023 and won it again today with 9-0; Haggas 4 of the last 5 (Ancestor 6th today). The race's own history said the top weight does not win this and the light-weighted horse from Balding or Haggas does — and the Signpost I built this morning reads ONE year back, which would have shown Tenability 8-12 and nothing more. Second time today the master has put the Past Winners table in front of me after a loss: the dot must read the last FIVE to TEN runnings, with the WEIGHT the winner carried, not just the name and SP. His word taken as given by the two pastes; it lands as tomorrow's cut, after the 09:30 page.
